topic: How does orbital altitude impact power and bandwidth efficiency in satellite constellations targeting underserved regions with 99% availability requirements?
consensus_response: Orbital altitude significantly impacts power and bandwidth efficiency in satellite constellations. At higher altitudes (e.g., GEO), signal attenuation due to atmospheric absorption increases, necessitating increased power transmission and bandwidth allocation. Conversely, lower altitudes (LEO) experience Doppler frequency offset/drift issues, requiring more complex user equipment designs. The choice of altitude affects coverage probability, data rate, power consumption, and interference, driving trade-offs between system performance and capacity.
reference_context: The reference context highlights the importance of evaluating trade-offs in satellite constellation design, particularly regarding altitude selection. Key parameters such as satellite altitude impact signal propagation, leading to increased path loss and latency at higher altitudes (GEO) and Doppler frequency offset/drift issues at lower altitudes (LEO).
